text:
sanjay: Quick follow-up from the console authz RFC — thinking out loud: what if we centralize policy evaluation into a tiny policy service instead of doing inline checks in the query panels? would address duplication across dashboard/panel/codepaths.
emma: I'm +1 on dedupe but worried about latency. query path is latency-sensitive (50-100ms tight tail). moving to svc adds hop.
li: can we do hybrid? fast-path inline cache for common allow/deny, fallback to policy svc for rare/complex rules.
sanjay: exactly. sketch: local LRU cache of compiled policy decisions per tenant+route, TTL short (2s), async refresh for warm entries; policy svc handles fallback + rule authoring.
emma: that TTL seems short but ok if local cache hits are super high. what about burst cold starts and thundering herd?
sanjay: mitigate with request coalescing and a per-instance in-flight map. also allow per-tenant warmers during rollout.
li: need to quantify cost: extra mem per instance (store keys + compiled decision blobs). Also adds operational surface area.
sanjay: yes — tradeoffs: less duplication (faster dev), single place to push policy changes, better audit logs. cons: svc ops, slightly higher tail if miss.
emma: another concern: consistency with dedicated/private deployments (on-prem). policy svc must be optional / embeddable. maybe expose a "local-mode" where the policy runtime can be embedded into the console process for air-gapped installs.
li: +1 for local-mode. also we should keep policy language intentionally small — no Turing-complete stuff; otherwise eval cost explodes.
sanjay: agreed. propose two concrete interfaces: 1) Decision API: /v1/decide { tenant, route, context } -> { decision, reason, version } 2) Management API for rules + versioning + canary rollouts. keep proto small.
emma: can we see a sample Decision API contract?
sanjay: sure — rough proto: 
``` 
POST /v1/decide
{ "tenant": "acme", "route": "console.panel.v1.render", "context": { "user_id": "u123", "token_scopes": ["read:dash"], "panel_meta": {"owner":"team-x"} } }
-> { "decision": "allow", "policy_id": "p-2025-07", "cache_ttl_ms": 2000, "explain": "scope match" }
```
li: include a stable decision_id and decision_version so console can correlate audit logs with tokens. important for forensics.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: note — any centralized policy svc increases blast radius. we should require HA across zones + circuit-breaker fallback. :warning:
emma: fallback behaviour is key: when policy svc is unreachable, we must have explicit degrade policy: default-deny vs default-allow is a product decision. we should recommend default-deny for sensitive routes and default-allow for low-risk telemetry views.
sanjay: propose route-level default behavior in policy manifest. UI should show last-known-policy-version and staleness. also surface stale-cache metric to console SLOs.
li: for perf tests, plan: microbench inline-vs-svc with simulated cache-hit/miss ratios (99th, 99.9th). include CPU/alloc deltas. want to see quant that embedding mode meets same tail.
sanjay: I'll draft an RCF follow-up doc with perf numbers and an API sketch. action items: (1) me: prototype local LRU + coalescing and measure 99.9th (2) emma: product to pick default-deny vs allow per tenant risk profile and document degrade UX (3) li: cost & memory model per console instance (4) ops-bot: add HA + circuit-breaker checklist to infra runbook.
emma: sounds good. can we also add a short eval plan for on-prem installers so they can opt into local-mode? we need clear ops steps.
sanjay: yes will include. thanks all. :thumbsup:
